memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'or if they touch human uncleanness (anything that would make them unclean) even though they are unaware of it, but then they learn of it and realise their guilt.'" - Lev 5:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Notice the phrase that keeps repeating through these verses: they realise their guilt. It appeared in verse 2. It appears again here. It will appear again in verse 4.

God builds His whole provision around that moment of realisation.

There is a kind of grace in being made aware. Before the realisation, the person carried the problem without knowing. Nothing could be done, because nothing was seen. The moment of recognition is the moment help becomes possible.

This is why conviction, uncomfortable as it feels, is a mercy. God is not exposing you to shame you. He is exposing you because the exposed thing can now be dealt with.

Many of us resist that moment. We deflect. We explain. We compare ourselves favourably to others. And in doing so we push away the very thing that would set us free. Whoever conceals their sins does not prosper, but the one who confesses and renounces them finds mercy (Prov 28:13).

David knew both sides of this. When I kept silent, my bones wasted away, he wrote. Then I acknowledged my sin to you and did not cover up my iniquity... and you forgave the guilt of my sin (Ps 32:3-5).

The realisation is not the punishment. It is the doorway.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there something God has been making me aware of that I keep pushing away?
2. Do I treat conviction as an enemy or as the beginning of freedom?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You show me what I could not see. Give me the honesty to face it rather than explain it away. Amen.
